Commentary.Commentary: It should be an interesting run chase. The Windies are stronger than the Aussies and will look to maximize the Powerplay. Australia's running between the wickets was not the best either, turning down plenty of twos. That might be a factor as well. Stay tuned to find out the first finalist.

Nothing much to write against the Windies. They started well, kept the pressure on consistently but just towards the end, they let it slip a little. Barring Fletcher, everyone was economical. Pace off was the key on this pitch and the trio of Taylor, Matthews and Fletcher went for 77 in 12 overs combined, for 3 wickets.

The Aussies had to grind their way out in the middle but credit to them for not throwing their wickets away. They could so easily have been 50/5 or 100/8 but the top order kept its cool. Healy and Lanning steadied the ship with a 51-run stand after the early dismissal of Mooney and then towards the end, Haynes's cameo of 25 from just 15 balls helped the visitors gain some momentum.

Excellent bowling display from the Windies. Take out the last 3 overs, which went for 29 - and it becomes a brilliant effort. They were up for this contest right from the start and never let Australia get away.
Short and outside off, dragged to deep mid-wicket for just one. WINDIES NEED 143 TO ENTER THE FINAL!
Short and outside off, Rachael looks to cut but is beaten due to the extra bounce.
FOUR! Excellent maneuvering of the field! Full and around middle, Haynes gets across and sweeps it over short fine leg for a boundary!
Drives this through the covers whee the fielder gets a hand to it and parries it wide of long off. A couple taken.
Now Perry jumps out and blasts it past the left hand of Taylor to long off for a run.
Comes down the track, takes it on the full and hits it down to long off for a single.
Down the leg side, nudged towards fine leg for one. 17 from that over, a bit of a momentum for Australia.
Outside off, pushed through point for a run.
Short and outside off, pulled to deep mid-wicket for just a single.
FOUR! Third boundary of the over! Down the leg side, the radar is loose once more and Haynes says thank you very much. Tucked to the fine leg fence.
WIDE. Pressure on Dottin now, gets it almost outside the pitch outside off. RH almost chases that too, bailing out in the end.
FOUR! Cheeky stuff. A low full toss outside off, Haynes looks to guide it to third man but ends up hitting it too fine. Just past the diving keeper, to the fence.
WIDE. Gets the line wrong this time, short and down the leg side, Rachael misses out on the pull.

FOUR! Tough luck for Shakera Selman. Short and around off, Haynes pulls it through mid-wicket. Selman races to her left, dives and stops the ball but while trying to push it back, her legs touch the ropes.
Short and outside off, pulled to long on for just one. Just 3 runs and a wicket from that over. Taylor's figures read 3-0-11-1.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Fuller on middle, pushed through mid on for a run.
Eases this through point for a single.
Full and outside off, Haynes looks to sweep but misses.
Finally, she is here. Not much time left. Just 17 balls to go. What can Ellyse Perry do?

OUT! Spectacular catch from Britney Cooper! Boy, have the Windies been brilliant on the field or what! A short ball, outside off, Villani goes back to pull but is done in by the slowness of the surface. She does not quite get enough on that and the ball dips on its way to deep mid-wicket. But Cooper runs in, keeps her eyes on the ball and dives to her right to pluck the ball inches off the surface!
Stafanie Taylor returns. 2-0-8-0 so far.
Full on middle, worked through mid-wicket for a run. 10 runs but a big wicket as well, from that over.
WIDE. Second one of the over. Villani moves well across her stumps and Dottin bowls it down the leg side. The batter misses her flick.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
WIDE. Full and miles outside off, Haynes reaches out to drive but misses.
Rachael Haynes is the new batter in at number 6, replacing her skipper.

OUT! Timber! Lanning departs now, at probably the worst possible stage for Australia. She was the set batter and needed to bat out the 20 overs, for the Aussies to get close to 140-150. Big blow. Backs away a month in advance and Dottin fires it on a length, around off. The ball moves in a touch and goes past the attempted inside-out shot of Meg. Crashes into the leg stump. Two new batters out there in the middle now.
A rare misfield. Full and outside off, Meg drives this through the covers where the fielder comes charging in but at the time of picking up the ball, fumbles. One is converted into two.

FOUR LEG BYES! It has not been Kycia Knight's day on the field. Down the leg side, Lanning misses her clip and the ball goes off her pads behind. Knight dives to her left, should have stopped that but the ball bursts through her gloves to the fine leg fence.
Landed outside off, guided straight to backward point.
The crowd cheers its throat out. Because... Deandra Dottin is about to bowl.

Short and outside off, cut through point where a brilliant stop ensures that it is a dot. A bit expensive, was Fletcher, 4-0-33-1, but she got the all-important wicket of Healy. At least robbed Australia off 15-20 runs.
Short and wide outside off, cut through point for one.
WIDE. Harsh call. Landed outside off, Lanning gets well across to cut but is beaten by the leg spin.
A short ball, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Beautifully tossed up outside off, Elyse looks to flick but is beaten by the away turn.
FOUR! Great shot to bring up a laboured 100 for Australia. Full and outside off, Villani gets down and across and sweeps this behind square leg to find the fence.
Full and outside off, heaved towards long on for a single.
Full and outside off, spinning in a long way, watchfully defended. Excellent spell from Matthews - 4-0-24-1.
Elyse Villani comes in next, at number 5, replacing Gardner.

OUT! Caught! Another wicket at the right time for the Windies. Full and outside off, Gardner comes down the track, looks to go over the mid off but the ball hits the top half of her bat. Easy catch to Chinelle Henry at mid off off the miscue.
Comes down the track, goes hard at the ball but it goes off the bat's inner half to deep backward square leg. A run taken.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Down the leg side, Meg gets across and looks to sweep but the ball goes off something towards fine leg. Was it glove? Naah... the umpire signals a leg bye.
FOUR! Another lofted shot. Full and outside off, Lanning steps out, gets to the pitch of the ball and lofts it over cover for a boundary.
SIX! Lovely shot to end the over. Difficult one to execute on this pitch. Full and outside off, Gardner comes down the track and lofts it over long on! 10 runs from that over.
Short and outside off, Gardner looks to cut but misses.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Around off, defended from the crease.

Full and outside off, Gardner comes down the track and looks to go over cover but skews it. The ball lands safely in the deep and the batters take a couple. While going for the second, Gardner nearly runs into Lanning and the skipper adopts a longer route to getting back.
WIDE. Landed outside off, spinning away a long way, left alone.
Full toss outside off, swept through mid-wicket for a single.
Another full toss, swiped through mid-wicket for a run.
Outside off, a full toss, slammed to long on for a single.

EDGED, DROPPED, FOUR! Nearly back-to-back wickets for the Windies. Not the start Gardner would have wanted but she will take it. Outside off, Ashleigh goes for the punch on the up but the ball spins in, takes the outside edge and goes behind. Kycia Knight is late in getting up again.
Outside off, driven to short cover again.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Poor running again. Full and outside off, Lanning opens the face of her bat and guides it to short third man. The non-striker was keen on the single but Lanning wasn't.
Ashleigh Gardner walks in at number 4, replacing Healy.

OUT! Caught! Healy departs and this is a massive wicket for Windies. Full and outside off, Alyssa gets across to sweep but the tennis-ball bounce does her in. She miscues her shot and the ball lobs off the top edge, straight to Shamilia Connell at short fine leg. The 51-run stand is broken and a crucial 46 from Healy comes to an end.
Full and floated miles outside off, Lanning gets well across and drives it through the covers for a run.
Comes down the track and bunts it to long on for a single.
Goes for the reverse pull this time, but misses.

FOUR! Even better from Healy. She is manipulating herself around the crease and this time, she gets across her stumps. Takes the ball on the full, well outside off and sweeps it through mid-wicket for consecutive boundaries.
FOUR! Smart and cheeky from Healy. Full and outside off, Alyssa brings out the reverse sweep and gets it past short third man!

Down the track comes Healy and swings it hard in the air. Does not quite get it right but the ball is in the gap. Deep square leg gets across to her left and Alyssa wants the second but Lanning refuses. Poor running.
Outside off, pushed straight to the bowler.
Full and outside off, swept powerfully but straight to deep mid-wicket for one.
Full on middle, pushed towards long on for a run.

FOUR! Street smart cricket from Healy. She is more known for going down the ground, doing power-hitting. Shows us her classy stuff too. Waits for the ball to come to her and dabs it pretty late, right from the keeper's gloves, to the third man fence.
Short and outside off, spinning in, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Gets well across her stumps and Fletcher tosses it up even further away, outside the wide guidelines. Healy cannot connect with her sweep. The squeeze is on from the Windies.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for one more.
Short again, cut again, just one more.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers. The call is for two but these Windies fielders are too quick. Just a run.
Sightscreen issues for Lanning.
Works it past the bowler towards long on for a run. 50 UP FOR AUSTRALIA, but the run rate is less than 6.
Full and outside off, steered through point for a single.
Afy Fletcher, the leggie, to bowl now.
Short ball, pulled straight to short mid-wicket. Eventful over.
Punches this past the bowler towards long on for one.
Outside off, slogged towards long on for a run.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.

SAFE AGAIN. Two in two for Lanning. Short and outside off, Meg opens the face of her bat and guides it through point. Deandra Dottin throws herself to her left and seeing that, Healy sends her skipper back who has to dive in. A run out is referred upstairs but replays show that the dive rescues the skipper again.
The third umpire is busy again! Is this a run out now?

SAFE. But what a take from the keeper. Full and flighted outside off, Lanning jumps out of the crease and looks to go big but misses. She then tries to dive back into the crease as Kycia Knight keeps her eyes on the ball, takes it with the turn and then whips off the bails. It is referred upstairs as Lanning looks towards the square leg umpire while the Windies are celebrating. However, replays show that the bat has just been plonked in, when the bails are off.
And do we have a stumping first ball? Lanning is walking. Referred upstairs...
Hayley Matthews into the attack now.
Full and outside off, squeezed out straight to short third man.
Dropped short, pulled through mid on for a run.

EDGED, DROPPED! Big deflection. Short and outside off, Healy looks to cut but gets a thick outside edge. Kycia Knight cannot get up in time and the ball goes off her gloves behind towards third man. A run taken.
Now the skipper uses her feet, gets to the pitch of the ball, takes it on the full and drives it straight to cover who fumbles and concedes a run. Tea pots boiling from Taylor.
Sees Healy advance and holds this back nicely through the air, full and wide outside off. Dragged down to long on for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and straight, watchfully defended. Selman's done with the ball for the day - 4-0-28-1.

FOUR! AUDACIOUS! There is the skipper for you. Full and around off, Lanning brings her bottom hand into play and whips it over mid on for a boundary. Not an easy shot to play on a slow surface, with the ball getting old. Woman power.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Outside off, on a length, punched through the covers for one.
Selman is not amused. Cannot allow a tip-and-run on this sticky surface. Outside off, Lanning just pushes this towards cover and runs off.
Full and around off, driven straight back.
Outside off, punched down to long on for a run. 35/1 IN THE POWERPLAY FOR AUSTRALIA - THEIR LOWEST IN THIS TOURNAMENT.
Pushes this straight to point.
Plenty of grip on this one. Landed outside off, drifting in a long way, Lanning is cramped for room as she tries to punch.
Waltzes down the track again, pushing the ball through cover for a single.
Cannot bowl there. Landed well outside off, spinning in, Healy waits for the ball to come and deftly guides it past the keeper through third man. Two runs taken.
Straightaway jumps out, driving the ball straight to cover.
First bowling change. First time, it is going to be pace off. Stafanie Taylor into the attack.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.

Desperate stuff from Shemaine Campbelle. Ohh... the Windies are up for this game alright. Full and outside off, Healy has a mow over mid-wicket, thanks to her strong bottom hand but the outfield holds up the ball. Campbelle runs back from mid-wicket and dives prematurely but manages to drag the ball back in. Three runs taken.
Full around off, pushed towards mid on for a quick one.
Around off, pushed straight to point.

Magnificent fielding! Deandra Dottin is the name. Full and wide outside off, Healy slices this behind point and almost gives a catch to the fielder who dives to her left and manages to half-stop the ball. A run taken.
Outside off, played towards third man for a single.
Outside off, played straight to point.

IN THE AIR... JUST CLEARS MID OFF! Nearly another wicket for the Windies. Nervy moment for Healy. A length ball outside off, Alyssa looks to hit this on the up over mid off but the shot comes way too early. This is not a hit-through-the-line pitch and AH almost pays the price for it. Chinelle Henry backtracks from mid off, tries to go one-handed to her right but the ball brushes her fingertips and goes down. A couple taken.
Fuller in length this time, outside off, Lanning gets it towards third man to be off the mark.
Lovely delivery, shaping back in, almost a yorker outside off, jammed towards mid off.
Outside off, played through the covers for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
A full toss, whipped uppishly but straight to short mid-wicket. Lands just short. A misfield ensures a single. 8 runs and a wicket from the over.
Meg Lanning comes in at number 3, replacing Mooney.

OUT! Caught at mid off! There is the first wicket of the semi-final and Selman gets the breakthrough. Full and around off, Beth walks down the track and looks to chip it over the top but the ball comes slowly off the surface again. She is early into the shot and only manages to spoon a simple catch to Natasha McLean moving to her left from mid off.
Full and outside off, chipped down to long off for a single.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.

SIX! ADMONISHED! Magnificent strike from Healy. A length ball outside off, Healy swings this over long on! There was a fielder placed at long off, so Alyssa chose the safer option to go aerial, in case she miscued.
Width on offer again, fuller in length outside off, Healy reaches out to drive but cannot quite get it in the gap. Straight to cover.
Much better from the bowler, gets it fuller, driven straight to cover.
IN THE AIR, JUST OVER! FOUR! Short and just around off, Mooney rocks back and pulls it over a leaping short mid-wicket for a boundary! The stand moves to 13 from 11 balls.
Action replay of the previous delivery. This time, Mooney wanted to get it behind point but could not quite do so.
Full and around off, pushed straight to point.
Landed outside off, this time Alyssa waits for the ball to come to her and runs it down to third man for a single.
Full and outside off, Healy plays this a touch uppishly and skews it towards cover.
Shamilia Connell to bowl from the other end.

MISCUE, BUT SAFE! Full and outside off, Alyssa looks to go over the top but the ball comes slowly off the surface and the batter miscues it. Luckily for her, long off cannot get to the ball. One run taken.
FOUR! WHOOSH! Mild concussion? Says who? Short and outside off, Healy rocks back and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary! The first of the match.
Dead ball. 'Oh security guard, please...' laments Ian Bishop on air. Selman was running in but that guard moved right in front of the sightscreen when Shakera was about to deliver. Healy bailed out.
Down the leg side, barely comes up to the batter, worked through square leg for one.
Outside off, holds up a little, Alyssa watchfully punches this through the covers for a run.
Australia and Mooney are away now. On a length outside off, Beth punches this through the covers, hesitates but Healy calls her through for the single.
Looks for a drop and run to kickstart things, but a very quick no from Alyssa Healy as the ball was just near the bowler, on the leg side.
The Windies now get into a huddle. Out come the Aussie openers - Beth Mooney and Alyssa Healy. Shakera Selman to take the new ball first up for the hosts. Mooney to face. Let's play!

'Rally... Rally 'round the West Indies...' has been sung and we are now ready for the first semi-final match to begin! Fasten your seat belts! Defending champions versus the runners-up in this first knockout. Here we go!
Time for the national anthems then. First up, it will be Australia.

PITCH REPORT - Anjum Chopra observes the pitch and says that it is a lovely toss to win for the Windies because the hosts have preferred restricting opponents to a small total and chasing that down. Feels that this is a belter of a track and one can expect a run fest.

Australian skipper, Meg Lanning, says that she was looking to bat any which ways. Cannot wait to get out in the middle after a long layoff. Does not think the pitch will change too much over the course of 40 overs. Informs that Alyssa Healy is fit and Georgia Wareham is back in the side. Adds that the Aussies are well prepared but also admits the fact that the Windies have been playing excellent cricket throughout the tournament.

Windies captain, Stafanie Taylor, says that the reason to bowl first is because there could be some juice on this wicket considering that it is a day game. Hence wants to make use of the early moisture. Agrees that the hosts have a really good bowling attack and wants to prove that today. On the team noise, Taylor says that she likes to be quiet while a few others in the side like to be vocal. Informs that the team is unchanged from the previous game.
TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin. Stafanie Taylor flips it in the air, HEADS is the call from Meg Lanning, but it is a TAIL. WINDIES WILL CHASE.
WEATHER - It is a pleasant, sunny day for cricket. No forecast for rain and we don't want any!

The hosts come into this contest pumped up, having won all their league games. The Aussies, on the other hand, have not been at their best and were badly exposed by India in their last league match. Will they bounce back from that defeat?

It is time for the final four of the 2018 WWT20! Windies, India, Australia and England are the names of those. Not too surprising, perhaps the only surprise would be the way South Africa and New Zealand got knocked out. We move on to a new venue - Antigua, where the remaining matches will be played. First up, a re-match of the 2016 WWT20 final. Hello and a warm welcome to the first semi-final between Windies and Australia.
